Consult Summary:
- Adult female with six days of dysuria, midline lower abdominal pain (7/10), and foul-smelling urine with spotting of blood; no fever reported.
- Clinical impression: likely acute urinary tract infection; plan includes a short course of antibiotics, hydration, and symptom management with follow-up if worse or not improving.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) likely.
  - Timeline: onset six days ago; dysuria with foul-smelling urine; midline lower abdominal pain; urine shows blood; pain constant but fluctuates; no fever.
  - Associated symptoms: no loin pain, no vaginal discharge, no weight loss; regular periods.
  - Systems review: negative for fever; no back pain; IBS history; no changes in bowel habit reported.
  - Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg taken three times daily; dose/route/frequency documented.
  - Allergies: Clindamycin.
  - Social history: lives with friends; works as a support worker; drinks alcohol occasionally (one glass per week); non-smoker.
  - Examination findings: not documented.
  - Differential/differential diagnosis: urinary tract infection suspected by clinician; no urine test performed at this time.
  - Specialist/allied health review: none referenced.

- Not applicable / No additional active clinical issues identified.

  - Note: Mebeverine dose/frequency documented.
- Antibiotics for suspected urinary tract infection:
  - Name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented; planned for a 3-day course.

Plan:
- Prescribe a 3-day course of antibiotics for suspected urinary tract infection (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); pharmacy to Knightsbridge Practice (via Babylon); pickup expected in about an hour (not immediate).
- Advise increased fluid intake: 2.5–3 liters of water per day.
- Suggest cranberry juice consumption.
- Suggest urine acidity sachets (as available from chemist/pharmacy).
- Instruct to check temperature at home with a thermometer; monitor for fever.
- Instructions to contact or seek reassessment if: pain worsens, fever develops, unable to pass urine, or symptoms do not resolve with treatment.
- If symptoms recur or become a recurrent problem, follow-up discussion recommended.
- No need to call after finishing antibiotics if symptoms resolve; return if symptoms worsen or persist.
